articles.title: LA 2028 triathlon course will see athletes race from Venice Beach into Pacific
articles.summary: Women’s triathlon will award first medals of Games. Beach start only second in Olympic triathlon history. The first medals of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics will be doled out on the eclectic confines of Venice Beach, where organizers have unveiled a triathlon course that will send athletes racing…
body: LA28 unveiled initial details of the Olympic and Paralympic triathlon routes on Wednesday, laying out a compact course through Venice that takes in the beachfront bike path, neighboring streets and the Venice Canals before finishing overlooking the coastline.

The women’s individual triathlon on 15 July 2028 will produce the first medals of the Games, one day after the unprecedented dual-venue opening ceremony at the the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum and SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. The men’s race follows on 16 July, with the mixed relay on 20 July.

In a departure from the usual Olympic setup, the individual races will begin on the beach rather than from a pontoon. It will be only the second beach start in Olympic triathlon history, following the 2016 events at Rio de Janeiro’s Copacabana Beach, with athletes sprinting from the sand directly into the Pacific. They will complete a two-lap 1,500m swim – an opening 1,000m circuit followed by a 25m run along the beach and a second 500m swim.

articles.title: Antonelli on 'stepping up' after 2024 crash 'stayed in my head for a very long time'
articles.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli tells BBC Sport how he is "still finding my way" in F1 after a 2024 crash "stayed in my head for a very long time".
body: Kimi Antonelli says he knew from the first moment he drove this year's Mercedes that he would be transformed as a Formula 1 driver in 2026.
The 20-year-old Italian, who is running away with the world championship in only his second season in F1, is reflecting on his breakthrough year in the sport in an exclusive interview with BBC Sport.

A difficult debut season last year had left external expectations of Antonelli low at the start of 2026. But on a typically damp and cold January day at Silverstone, he already sensed that something special might be on the cards.

"It was just a few laps in the wet," Antonelli says, "but I just felt better in the car, much better than I felt last year. Also the car felt well, but I just felt better mentally in the car. Less tense, more relaxed and more mature."

articles.title: Manchester United report seventh straight annual loss despite record revenue
articles.summary: Net loss of £43m for year ended 30 June 2026. Revenue hits £677.6m and forecast to grow again. Manchester United reported their seventh straight annual ⁠loss on Wednesday as costs related to player acquisitions and January’s sacking of Ruben Amorim pushed them ⁠deeper into ​the red.
body: The wider loss comes despite drastic actions taken by the British billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the club’s minority shareholder and ⁠head of their football operations, to revive profitability, including by cutting jobs and raising ticket prices.
United reported a net loss of £43m for the year ended 30 June 2026, wider than £33m a year ​ago, incurring an exceptional cost of £8.2m related to Amorim’s ‌departure as head coach and restructuring.

The loss came despite record revenue of £677.6m – up 1.7%. United’s New York-listed shares, which have gained almost 24% this ‌year, were down 3% in US premarket trading. The 20-times English champions have racked up losses of nearly £190m since fiscal 2024.
“We will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable,” the CEO, Omar Berrada, ​said in a statement.

articles.title: Florian Wirtz does not look like a £116m player but it is early to write him off
articles.summary: The 23-year-old playmaker has been disappointing for Liverpool but has he really been that bad? By Opta Analyst. When Florian Wirtz signed for Liverpool in the summer of 2025, there was only one logical assumption.
body: Football has a habit of flipping the script, though. Last season was difficult for Liverpool for several reasons, and Wirtz, along with other new arrivals, struggled to make the impact expected of a £116m player. There were conversations among fans this summer about how long he and fellow nine-figure signing Alexander Isak should be given before difficult questions needed be asked. The consensus was until Christmas.

As it turned out, the real answer was after the opening game as Wirtz and Isak laboured in Liverpool’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle and loud doubts began to surface. Jamie Carragher spoke on the first Monday Night Football of the season about Wirtz’s signing in 2025 potentially being part of the “worst transfer window in Premier League history”.

The former Liverpool defender was criticising a few players – and Isak has since gone on to score four times in his last four league appearances to quieten his doubters – but Carragher focused his ire on Wirtz again on Sunday in a new podcast for Sky Sports.

articles.title: Man Utd still £1bn in debt with £63.5m spent on new stadium
articles.summary: Manchester United's overall debt remains over £1bn despite Sir Jim Ratcliffe's extensive cost-cutting measures, with the club also confirming it has spent £63.5m buying land for their new stadium.
body: Amid a backdrop of fan protests and a disappointing start to the season that has left United 12th in the Premier League and already out of the EFL Cup, United have announced record revenues of £677.6m and a £22.6m operating profit despite not playing in Europe for the first time in a decade.
However, while they have saved £8.5m of a projected £16.5m pay-off to axed boss Ruben Amorim after he accepted a job at AC Milan, other costs have increased.

Net finance costs for the year were £69.6m, an increase of 228.3%. United put most of this down to a foreign exchange loss. According to football finance expert Kieran Maguire, this sum alone has now exceeded £1bn since the leveraged Glazer family buyout in 2005.

In addition, United also confirmed they spent £63.5m of an additional $125 (£94.14m) added to their historic debt during a summer refinancing move on land for their new stadium. The club has not explained what it has done with the remainder. The stadium itself is likely to cost in excess of £2bn.

She has been deployed at right-back in the opening three games of the season for Liverpool and comes back into the Scotland ranks for next month's Women's World Cup round one two-legged play-off against the Czech Republic.

"She was close before the season ended, but it was just the timing of things, where we were in our preparations as well," the head coach said after naming her squad, which also involves Newcastle United striker Martha Thomas for the first time since October, when she earned her 50th cap.

articles.title: Video shows police point Taser at Paige Bueckers during Arike Ogunbowale's March arrest
articles.summary: Body camera footage from the Miami Police Department showed that an officer pointed a Taser at former UConn women's basketball star Paige Bueckers, according to a California Post report.
body: The footage was recorded during the arrest of Dallas Wings teammate Arike Ogunbowale on the morning of March 5, after players celebrated Ogunbowale and Mist BC winning the 2026 Unrivaled championship.

In the video obtained by the Post, which reportedly took place outside the Miami nightclub E11EVEN, Bueckers had her arms around Ogunbowale and can be heard saying, "We got her." The officer responded by instructing Bueckers to remove her hands from Ogunbowale and raised the Taser toward the former UConn star.

Ogunbowale was seen being placed into handcuffs on the body camera footage and was arrested around 4:20 a.m., according to Miami-Dade County records cited by ESPN. The four-time WNBA All-Star was charged with misdemeanor battery after authorities alleged she punched a nightclub security guard in the face, but the prosecution withdrew the criminal charge in May before the case went to trial.

articles.summary: Juventus have shown really good form in their last two matches, providing renewed belief that they can enjoy a successful season. Their recent results have also lifted the mood among their supporters, who will be hoping the team can maintain its momentum after the international break.
body: The Bianconeri had previously dropped points in back-to-back league games, results that brought back some of the negative feelings their fans had experienced during some of the club’s worst campaigns. That difficult spell raised questions about whether Juventus could compete consistently across the season.
However, Juve responded positively in their next matches. They thrashed NEC 5-0 in the Europa League before beating Atalanta in Serie A shortly before the international break.
Those results have given the team a stronger platform to build on, and supporters will expect Juventus to continue from where they stopped when domestic and European action resumes.

articles.title: Sky Sports to show England men's tour of South Africa this winter
articles.summary: Sky Sports and Cricket South Africa have extended their longstanding partnership, with Sky Sports and NOW to exclusively broadcast the England men's three-Test and three-ODI tour of South Africa this winter.
body: England's three-Test series against South Africa will take place across December and January, marking England's first Test tour of South Africa in seven years.
The series follows England's first-ever home Test series whitewash of Pakistan and will be Stephen Fleming's first series in charge as England men's Test head coach.

The Test series will be followed by three ODIs in January, as England prepare for the ICC Men's World Cup 2027, which will take place across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia in October and November next year.

Sky Sports will broadcast live coverage of a packed schedule of international cricket from South Africa, with Australia men's tour getting under way this Thursday with the first of three ODIs in Durban, followed by three Tests.

articles.title: Can Arteta turn champions into serial winners?
articles.summary: When Mikel Arteta signed his last Arsenal contract in September 2024, his quest to bring major silverware back to the club was ongoing. Two years later, he agrees his new one after leading them to a long-awaited Premier League title.
body: Mikel Arteta has agreed a new contract as Arsenal manager following their Premier League title triumph last season; Gunners boss has overseen a remarkable transformation of the club since his arrival in 2019, so can he build on their success?

Arteta has overseen a total transformation of the club since his appointment in 2019. Arsenal, 10th in the Premier League table when he took over, were in a state of drift. Now, they are re-established among Europe's elite, unrecognisable in all departments.

Arteta has joined a select group of 13 managers to have won the Premier League. He now has the chance to join an even smaller group, made up of only Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho and Arsene Wenger, by winning it more than once.
Securing a first Champions League, after guiding Arsenal to only their second final last term, is another chance for immortality.
